title: Apartment backflow testing: manage units, common systems, and records
description: Apartment testing succeeds when common-area or building assets are clearly mapped, access is arranged, the eligible tester is scheduled, and each completed.
prompt: Which apartment assets, access rules, and records belong in the testing cycle?
answer: Apartment testing succeeds when common-area or building assets are clearly mapped, access is arranged, the eligible tester is scheduled, and each completed result is filed against the correct assembly. Unit count is not a device count.
urgency: Escalate missing asset records, tenant access issues, shared water-system uncertainty, or a deadline without a repair window.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: List each assembly by building, location, model, size, and last result.
Separate common-area devices from any tenant-controlled access point.
Assign a property contact who can authorize access and receive failures.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Map responsibility
steps.body: Build the device list before scheduling.

steps.title: Operate the workflow
steps.body: Coordinate building access and repair authorization with site contacts.

steps.title: Retain the proof
steps.body: File results and retain asset-specific proof for each assembly.

safeChecks: Verify asset identity and access responsibility before scheduling.
Use the official program requirement for tester and filing rules.
Keep the final record with the property or facility asset file.
stopConditions: No one can confirm which devices are in scope.
A failed result has no repair authority or access plan.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: The official program controls testing and filing; exact manufacturer records control the identified assembly service path.
